newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. offers no easing of Israeli sanctions - PLO.
newsitem.headline: U.S. offers no easing of Israeli sanctions - PLO.

text.p: A Palestinian cabinet minister said a U.S. peace envoy meeting President Yasser Arafat on Wednesday had failed to report any plans by Israeli leader Benjamin Netanyahu to ease sanctions on Palestinians.

Speaking at a PLO function after attending the meeting with Arafat and envoy Dennis Ross in the self-ruled West Bank town of Ramallah, Planning Minister Nabil Shaath said: "Ross came tonight with almost nothing from Mr Netanyahu."

"We have to continue suffering from a siege for a crime we have not committed. Mr Netanyahu gave him (Ross) nothing on that front," Shaath told a dinner in Ramallah for a visiting South African minister.
Israel clamped a closure on the territories after a July 30 attack at a Jerusalem market claimed the lives of 16 people, including two suicide bombers.

After meeting Arafat at the end of a four-day mission, Ross had said he believed some of the measures which Israel had imposed on Palestinians following the attack, particularly a closure on the West Bank and Gaza Strip, would be eased. But he did not say when.
Netanyahu, speaking after talks with King Hussein in Jordan, said he was ready to relax a closure of the West Bank and Gaza as soon as Palestinians crushed "terrorists" behind the suicide bombings.
